break_glass.notes: Admin overrides MUST be exceptional, time-bounded, and auditable.

capabilities_required.description: Read effective consent for a subject_key.
Create grant proofs for a subject_key.

new_proposed_invariant.statement: NEW: proposed invariant — IAM MUST expose capability IDs consent_read, consent_write, consent_withdraw, consent_proof_read with org-scoped enforcement.

extension_rules.notes: Custom purposes MUST be org-scoped and MUST start with org_. Example: org_newsletter_opt_in.

minimum_set.description: Strictly necessary for core functionality and security (authentication, fraud prevention, transaction integrity).
Measurement and product analytics that are not strictly necessary.
Convenience features that store user preferences beyond core necessity.

new_proposed_invariant.statement: NEW: proposed invariant — user-provided region override MUST NOT result in a less restrictive profile than the geo-inferred profile.

rules: If explicit_user_region_override exists, it MUST be used ONLY when it results in equal or higher restrictiveness than request_geo_inference.
If request_geo_inference is missing or low-confidence, unknown_strict MUST be used.

minimum_set.description: Most restrictive default for EU/EEA/UK and unknown geos.
Default profile for South Africa unless overridden by org policy.
Fallback when region cannot be confidently determined.

deterministic_steps: Load org_policy for org_id (if present); org_policy MAY specify per-region default profiles and per-purpose overrides.
Compute baseline decision per purpose from effective_region_profile defaults, then apply org_policy overrides.
Apply global_privacy_control (gpc) as a deny for all non-necessary purposes when present.
Apply withdrawals as deny for the withdrawn purposes, effective immediately.
For each purpose_id: if any input yields deny, effective MUST be deny; else if at least one yields allow and none yield deny, effective MUST be allow; else unset yields baseline.
Emit a deterministic consent_evaluation record (hashable) for downstream enforcement.
tie_breakers: necessary MUST always resolve to allow unless the request is explicitly blocked for security reasons outside consent scope.
unknown_strict MUST win over any less restrictive baseline if any ambiguity exists.

hashing.notes: evaluation_hash_sha256 MUST be computed over RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalized consent_evaluation without volatile transport fields.

dependencies.reason: Constitutional invariants (multi-tenancy, immutability posture, reliability posture).
Tenant isolation invariants (org_id scoping, RLS posture, session GUC name).
Outbox requirements for reliable, idempotent consent-change propagation (no direct side effects).
SEC-1 crypto controls plus explicit RFC 8785 (JCS) semantics for deterministic proof hashing/signing.
Retention, archival, and deletion semantics for proofs and derived state.
Event Registry head pin for Phase 5 parity (consent events).
Normalized schema_ref token authority for event envelope validation.
Session/actor context dependency for consent policy evaluation.

subject_resolvability.resolution_mechanism: subject_id is the canonical opaque handle; pseudonym hashes are internal-only.
subject_resolvability.text: CONSENT MUST only emit consent events with subject_id values that are resolvable by IAM within the same org_id scope.

payload_minimization.notes: subject_key MUST NOT be emitted; subject_key_hash MUST be emitted instead.

normative_source: V42 Enterprise Ticketing — contract-first; Ash 3.x concepts only; root namespace Ticketing; OTP app :ticketing.

immutability_rules: Consent proofs MUST NOT be updated in-place.
Consent proofs MUST NOT be deleted except via ARCH-1 governed retention/archival processes.
Any change MUST be represented as a new proof record.

verification_requirements: On write: platform MUST verify prev_proof_hash_sha256 matches latest proof for org_id + subject_key (or null for first).
On read: platform MUST verify hash chain continuity for any returned sequence when requested with include_integrity=true.
Signature MUST be validated using a key managed per SEC-1; private keys MUST NOT be stored in the same database as proofs.

definitions.consent: Server-authoritative policy decision for a purpose on a subject_key in an org_id scope at a point in time. Consent is evaluated by the platform, not trusted from the client.
definitions.purpose_id: Stable snake_case identifier representing a category/purpose of processing.
definitions.subject_key: Pseudonymous stable identifier representing a data subject in a given org_id scope. It MUST NOT be raw PII (email, phone, id_number).

does_not_own: ui/ux (cookie banners, UI copy, styling, vendor widgets)
tracking implementation details (storage, cookies, device IDs) beyond enforcement requirements
dsar workflow implementation (handled by DSAR/ARCH subsystem), beyond integration obligations
regional legal interpretation (contract encodes suite policy, not legal advice)

summary: Single authority for consent purposes/categories, region profiles, deterministic resolution, append-only proofs with integrity, withdrawal semantics, and non-bypass enforcement hooks for any tracking/communication/integration subsystem.

new_proposed_invariant.statement: NEW: proposed invariant — org_id MUST NOT be null; platform-wide consent MUST be represented by a dedicated platform org_id.

rls_posture.notes: RLS MUST be enforced on consent proofs and derived state.

title: CONSENT-1 Consent Registry, Resolution, Proofs, and Enforcement Hooks

mandatory_for_any_subsystem: Any subsystem attempting processing for a purpose_id MUST present a consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 proving evaluation under this contract version.
If consent_evaluation_hash_sha256 is missing, the subsystem MUST fail closed with CONSENT_EVALUATION_REQUIRED.
non_bypass_guardrail: Client-provided consent flags MUST be treated as hints only; server MUST recompute effective consent.
Any attempt to persist identifiers for analytics/marketing when effective decision is deny MUST be rejected.

semantics: Withdrawal MUST be represented by a new proof record with record_kind=withdraw.
Withdrawal MUST take effect immediately for downstream enforcement (no grace period).
Previously collected data MUST NOT be retroactively re-consented; retention/deletion is governed by ARCH-1/DSAR workflows.
